svg.text: What happens when assembleFilingContent(ticker, dataPacket, env) is called
Runs after DataPacket assembly -- feeds filing text + transcripts to annual-reader and quarterly-reader agents
const dataPacket = await assembleDataPacket(ticker, env); // already done (see datapacket-assembly-flow.svg)
const filingResult = await assembleFilingContent(ticker, dataPacket, env);
{ form, filingDate, accessionNumber, primaryDocument } (no CIK -- use companyInfo.cik)
Annual reports -- Business, Risk Factors, MD&A, Financial Statements
Quarterly reports -- Financial Statements, MD&A, Risk Factors
(batches of 3 via Promise.allSettled -- up to 9 filings total)
Filings are immutable -- cached permanently. Cache HIT skips Steps 2b-2d, jumps to 2e.
CIK from dataPacket.companyInfo.cik | Direct fetch with User-Agent: 'Thes1s/1.0' | No proxy needed (Worker-side)
10-Ks can be 5-30MB HTML. .txt filings pass through as-is (normalize line endings only).
REMOVE: script, style, link, meta + all style/class attrs
Turndown + GFM plugin (uses built-in domino DOM server-side)
Custom table rule (pipe-delimited) | Font tag unwrap | Empty link cleanup | Blank line collapse
Imported from: src/engines/fileSections.js (pure regex -- Worker-safe, no changes needed)
Business | Risk Factors | MD&A | Financial Statements
TRUNCATION: 10-K sections capped at 40,000 chars | 10-Q sections capped at 15,000 chars
STEP 3: Fetch Transcripts (4 most recent quarters)
R2 key pattern: transcripts/COST/2024/Q4.json | Stored by cron job (api/src/cron/transcripts.js)
Sort by year/quarter desc, take 4 most recent
Parse JSON: { text, meta } -- return .text field
Key rotation: key1 / key2 alternated per call
AV results cached in R2 for future runs
STEP 4: Return to pipeline.js -- merge into DataPacket
'10-K-2024-09-28': { form, filingDate, sections: { Business, Risk Factors, ... }, charCount }
'10-Q-2024-06-30': { form, filingDate, sections: { Financial Statements, MD&A, ... }, charCount }
First run: ~10-20s (SEC downloads bottleneck, 10-Ks are 5-30MB HTML)
Cached runs: ~3-5s (R2 markdown retrieval, no SEC fetch)
